stories.headline: What's next for Man City? Appeals, possible punishments, how long it could take
stories.summary: Man City have appealed the Premier League's guilty verdict, while the sanctions board also begins its work on figuring out appropriate punishments. So what happens next, and what is the possible timeline?
stories.body:
Manchester City have lodged their appeal against an independent commission's guilty verdict of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-season period, and the waiting game now begins again for the final outcome of the investigation.

But the judgment of the independent panel -- made up of judges and independent financial and legal experts -- which was published on Sept. 29, 21 months after the culmination of a 12-week hearing, marked the end of the beginning of an investigative process dating back to 2019.

The appeal process heralds the beginning of the end, and sources have told ESPN that a time frame is in place for City's fate -- guilty or innocent -- to be resolved by the end of this season.

The club, which continues to protest its innocence citing "irrefutable evidence," could yet take the case beyond sporting regulatory bodies to the High Court in the United Kingdom if the appeal fails and City can prove serious irregularities in the Premier League's disciplinary process.

- Man City found guilty: All features, analysis, reaction

But now that City's appeal has been set in motion, both the club and Premier League are approaching the end of a long and difficult road. So what happens next? When will this all be over and what are the sanctions that City could face?

The appeals process

Man City had 14 days after being officially informed of the verdict from the independent commission to serve notice of their decision to appeal. The club did so on Oct 2. A new three-person independent panel, appointed by Sir Gary Hickinbottom (High Court judge and former UK Lord Justice of Appeal), will be formed as an Appeal Board to review the case.

In Premier League regulations, under Section W of the Premier League Handbook, Appeal Boards must have three members, one of whom should have held judicial office (a judge) and would sit as the chair of the Appeal Board.

The appeal process must be concluded within 12 weeks of the appeal being lodged. If the full 12 weeks are required to hear City's case, it would have to finish by Dec. 25 and the panel must deliver its verdict, according to Premier League regulation W.95, "within 30 days of the final day of the appeal hearing."

This is where the time frame gets tricky. The Christmas and New Year period will signal a two-week holiday shutdown of the legal process, so if the 30-day clock began on Jan. 8, the three-person panel would have until Feb. 8 to announce its verdict.

However, an appeal is not certain. The Appeal Board, as per regulation W.96, must initially decide whether to allow the appeal or dismiss it, but even if City's grounds for appeal are regarded as flimsy, it is unlikely that they would have it rejected due to the magnitude of the case.

The sanctions hearing

The original independent panel will meet to decide on the sanctions that should be applied to City. This process will be separate from the Appeal Board, but while there is no official time frame, sources said that it will likely run parallel to the appeal to ensure a swift application of penalties in the event of City failing to win their appeal.

As a result, we should have a final verdict and the application of sanctions by mid-February at the latest.

So what are the possible sanctions?

These are explained in section W.64 of the Premier League Handbook, ranging from a reprimand (W64.1) to the ultimate sanction of expulsion from the Premier League (W64.4.4 -- yes, there are four sub-clauses attached to sub-clause 64.4).

W.64.2 allows for an "unlimited fine," W.64.4.2 applies to points deductions, while W.64.7 allows for the commission to "impose upon the Respondent [City] any combination of the foregoing or such other penalty as it shall think fit." If the commission decides that City should be expelled from the Premier League, the 20 member clubs would vote on whether to accept the sanction and it would require a minimum of fifteen clubs to vote "yes."

A key thing to note: The commission decides on the sanction and the clubs must ratify it, as opposed to the clubs sitting around a table to decide the sanction.

Is expulsion from the Premier League really likely?

First of all, if City's guilt is upheld by the Appeal Board, a massive fine will be levied. Sources have told ESPN that it could be as high as £500 million due to the prolonged natured of the rule-breaking -- Premier League CEO Richard Masters said in the league's statement that City had "systematically broken the rules for nearly a decade."

Neither City nor the Premier League has commented to ESPN about the case and potential sanctions. As for expulsion, club sources within the Premier League and EFL (English Football League, which governs the English Championship, League One and League Two) have told ESPN that they expect City to be outside the top division as a consequence of the findings if their guilt is upheld.

The clean option would be to issue a points deduction so big -- at least 60 points -- that it would be impossible for City to avoid relegation to the Championship. But many within the game do not believe a one-tier relegation would be enough for City's rule-breaking, and that opens up the door to expulsion.

If City are kicked out of the Premier League, they would have to apply to join the EFL, and that would mean starting again in League Two. If the EFL rejected City, the next step would be the National League and all the way down until the bottom level of the English football pyramid at Tier 9.

This would be the nightmare scenario for City. Tier 9 would see them playing in the North-West Counties Football League First Division (North) against teams like Uppermill, Squires Gate and Maine Road FC -- a Manchester-based team, named after City's previous stadium, formed by City supporters in 1955.

ESPN visited Maine Road this week to assess the prospects of City starting out so far down the pyramid, but the lack of infrastructure and facilities would make it a nonstarter due to teams and grounds at that level being ill-equipped to deal with a game against a club with such a large fan base.

Sources have told ESPN, however, that City, who had a season in League One as recently as 1998-99, would almost certainly be accepted into the EFL by a large majority of its 72 teams.

"The commercial directors in the EFL will be delighted by the prospect of a home game against City and the financial windfall that would bring," an EFL Championship club official told ESPN. "Every team and the EFL as a whole would get a financial and profile boost from having City involved, so I'm certain they would be voted into the league.

"It would be a fairly easy thing to do. Have two teams relegated from the Premier League, drop City into League Two and then adjust the promotion and relegation numbers in the EFL as required."

All 72 EFL clubs are due to meet on Oct. 22 for a preplanned summit, but according to the Championship source, "having City in the EFL will be a big topic of conversation."

After the sanctions, will there be another appeal?

Yes. If City's appeal fails and they are hit with a raft of punitive sanctions by the commission, they will be able to appeal against the punishments imposed. Everton had a 10-point penalty for breaching Premier League regulations reduced to six on appeal in February 2024, while Leicester City (April 2026) and Nottingham Forest (May 2024) both failed to overturn points deductions on appeal.

City would have another two-week period after being sanctioned to lodge an appeal and the process would start again -- a 12-week hearing and a 30-day period for the panel to announce its findings.

Let's say that Feb. 8 proves to be the day City get their sanctions; they would have to lodge an appeal against sanctions by Feb. 22. If an appeal process lasted the full 12 weeks, it would not conclude until May 17, just 13 days before the Premier League finishes on May 30. A 30-day period for the panel to announce its verdict would take the process beyond the end of the season -- potentially as late as June 17.

ESPN contacted the Premier League to ask whether a final sanction, issued in mid-June after the end of the league season, would apply to the 2026-27 season or held over until the 2027-28 season. But the league declined to comment beyond saying that the process is "private and confidential."

So, the clock is ticking. Due to the less-detailed nature of an appeal process against any possible sanction, it could run shorter than the appeal against the commission's findings, but the Premier League vs. Manchester City battle has run for seven years and is entering an eighth.

While the end is in sight, nobody can say for certain whether it will end this season or next.

stories.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Start Bucky Irving, sit Emeka Egbuka on Thursday night
stories.summary: Which Buccaneers should you start, sit or monitor coming into a Thursday night matchup with the Cowboys?
stories.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Oct. 8: Thursday preview and more league notes

By Michael F. Florio

Baker Mayfield remains out for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, which means rookie Jalon Daniels will start once again. Last week, Daniels threw for 148 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while running for 55 yards. His rushing ability and the favorable matchup have him as a deeper option in superflex leagues. Outside of that, go in another direction. Bucky Irving is the only Buccaneer that can be started with any confidence, as the Dallas Cowboys have allowed 97 rushing yards per game to running backs and four rushing touchdowns, the fourth most in the NFL. Try to stay away from Emeka Egbuka if possible.

Also, just a reminder to put your TNF and London players in your RB or WR spots and save your flex spots for players in later games. That provides you more flexibility just in case one of your players is a late scratch.

Week 5 stats to know

David Montgomery has posted career lows in yards per carry, forced missed tackles rate, explosive run rate, yards before and after contact per carry, average speed and success rate. Simply put, outside of the three TDs in Week 1, it's been rough for Monty. Wait for his next big game, which could be this week against the Tennessee Titans, and then look to trade him.
Carnell Tate's target share has climbed every week, reaching 43% in Week 4. He is being used downfield more. It seems like the Titans are unlocking him. On the season, 26 of his 32 targets have come against zone coverage, which the Houston Texans play 83% of the time.
Every QB who faced the Detroit Lions has scored at least 21 fantasy points. They have weekly finishes of QB8, QB1, QB3 and QB6. Start Jacoby Brissett this week.
Three of four QBs to face the Washington Commanders have topped 23 fantasy points. Jameis Winston is in play as a streaming option this week.
The Lions have allowed the most yards before contact per carry (2.0) and the second-highest explosive run rate (15%) to RBs. Jeremiyah Love is poised for a bounce-back performance.
Quinshon Judkins saw a career-high seven targets last week and his touches have increased every game, reaching 23 in Week 4. The New York Jets have allowed the fourth-most rushing yards per game to RBs.
Garrett Wilson has a 50% target share against man coverage, which is tied for the highest in the NFL (Amon-Ra St. Brown). The Cleveland Browns play man coverage at the highest rate in the NFL (50%).
DK Metcalf is tied for the league lead with 10 deep targets. This week he faces the Indianapolis Colts, who have allowed the most yards on deep passes.
Isaiah Likely has a 33% target share with Winston at QB. He faces the Commanders, who are in the top five in terms of most touchdowns and fantasy PPG allowed to tight ends.
Dalton Kincaid, who has just five targets and 45 yards in his last two games combined, faces the Los Angeles Rams who have allowed a league-low 85 yards to tight ends this season and just one touchdown.

Oct. 7: Trade for or trade away? SOS says make these six moves today

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

We're at that time of season where the fantasy football trade market is either heating up or is already at peak temperature.

There's inevitably a 0-4 team in your league, grasping to hopes of a miracle comeback. And it can be done, especially if I remind you that all you probably need is a 7-3 hot streak to make the playoffs as an I-sure-don't-want-to-face-them No. 4 seed. Trades -- especially bigger, badder and bolder ones -- are the best way to turn around a slow start.

One way to unearth the highest-ceiling trades is to lean heavily upon the upcoming schedule. Mix and match your way into the playoffs and be that maddening team to face! This week, Mike Clay has released his initial version of the rest-of-season schedule rankings at each position -- kickers and defenses, too!

It's a great tool for determining how fluky your player's extreme hot-or-cold start to the season might have been, as well as which players are in the best positions to thrive over the remaining 13 weeks of the fantasy season.

Here are six trade-related takeaways to consider as you start offering deals:

Bryce Young has been an unexpected early breakthrough, going from a No. 186 overall ADP and 11.1% opening-week roster rate to scoring the third-most fantasy points among quarterbacks through four weeks. He has certainly capitalized upon a soft schedule, the seventh-best at the position thus far. Young and his Carolina Panthers are on bye, but they have the position's third toughest the rest of the year. Young might be a tough player to trade based upon his past history, but considering his schedule and how bruised and battered the quarterback position on the whole, he's a name worth floating if you're confident in your QB1.
He might seem like an unappealing fantasy RB2, but Aaron Jones Sr. could be one of the sneakiest running back values amongst that valuation tier, particularly over the next six weeks. Since Jordan Mason landed on IR, Jones' 78% snap and 73% rushing shares both rank fourth, and his 41.5 fantasy points are 14th, among running backs. Jones and the Minnesota Vikings also face the third most-favorable remaining schedule at the position, including nothing but upper-half matchups (aside from a Week 6 bye) the next seven weeks (@NO, bye, IND, @DET, BUF, @GB, @SF).
Colston Loveland's fantasy managers are surely displeased after the No. 37 overall pick in terms of ADP has placed just 19th in target share (14.9%) and 31st in fantasy points (20.1) among tight ends through four weeks. His Chicago Bears' remaining schedule offers some hope of recovering TE1 value, as theirs has been the third toughest at the position thus far but the third most-favorable the rest of the year. Examining alternatives, I can't find more than five tight ends (Trey McBride, Brock Bowers, George Kittle, Tyler Warren and Sam LaPorta) I'd clearly prefer to Loveland the rest of the year.
It's difficult to envision Christian McCaffrey having as strong a finish as he had in 2025. The San Francisco 49ers have been more conservative with his workload through four weeks in 2026 (67% snap and 43% rushing shares) than at the same point in 2025 (83% and 65%), and he faces the most challenging remaining schedule among running backs. This isn't to persuade McCaffrey's managers to swiftly trade him for whatever they can get, but rather to caution that he might fall shy of expectations. Adjust your running back plan accordingly.
The hype surrounding Trevor Lawrence exiting Week 1 has dissipated, but there's still a lot to like about him and his receivers moving forward. Remember, Lawrence scored the second-most fantasy points among all players (and the most among quarterbacks) from Week 5 forward last year, and two of his toughest matchups all year are already in the rearview (Week 2-3's @DEN, NE). Between him and 2-fantasy-points-in-Week 4 WR Parker Washington, they're among my favorite trade targets right now.
The Seahawks' defense has again excelled early, their 40 fantasy points second among D/STs. What lies ahead, though, is the worst schedule for a defense, including two games apiece against the Los Angeles Rams and 49ers, and single meetings with the Kansas City Chiefs, Chicago Bears and Dallas Cowboys. Here's your almost daily reminder: Stream defenses!

Oct. 6: Jalen Hurts' job gets a lot tougher with Lane Johnson retirement

By Michael F. Florio

Lane Johnson announced his retirement from the NFL on Tuesday. That will leave a massive hole on the offensive line for an Eagles team that is missing a ton of star players. Saquon Barkley hurt a hamstring, and he is expected to miss Week 5. DeVonta Smith was out last week due to a hamstring injury, and he seems unlikely for Week 5. And Dallas Goedert remains sidelined with a knee injury.

Jalen Hurts has struggled in games without Johnson, having averaged 174 passing yards and 1.1 passing touchdowns per game when Johnson sat. On top of that, the quarterback faces a Jacksonville Jaguars team that has allowed three passing touchdowns and has six interceptions this season. Jacksonville can get after the QB, as well, producing 10 sacks through four weeks, eighth most in the NFL. That's problematic without Johnson.

Perhaps Hurts' rushing ability saves the day, but he has not ran as much this season. He has fewer than 20 rushing yards in two of his past three games and one rushing touchdown this campaign. Plus, the Jaguars have allowed the second-fewest rushing yards and just two rushing touchdowns so far in 2026.

Some QBs I would play over Hurts are Matthew Stafford, Jacoby Brissett, Kyler Murray and Jordan Love. The "floors" here are not safe, but Jameis Winston and Aaron Rodgers are upside options this week in favorable matchups.

Falcons' offense has come alive under Michael Penix Jr.

By Michael F. Florio

The Atlanta Falcons are hitting their stride with Michael Penix Jr. They scored 45 points Monday night against the New Orleans Saints and have 80 total in Penix's two starts. Penix threw for 223 yards and one touchdown, finishing with 12.72 fantasy points. He has yet to crack 15 and is primarily a superflex option, although all the QB injuries could change that.

Penix's impact on the Falcons offense cannot be overstated. Bijan Robinson went for 147 total yards and two touchdowns Monday, and in 16 career games with Penix at the helm he has 2,181 scrimmage yards and 17 touchdowns. Robinson saves his best for primetime, which means fantasy managers are in luck, as the Falcons play the Baltimore Ravens on "Sunday Night Football" next week.

Penix also continues to elevate Drake London. After going for 194 yards in Week 3, London was held to a modest 96 yards on five catches Monday. He has 105 catches, 1,576 yards and nine touchdowns in 16 career games with Penix. He has to be viewed as an elite fantasy option as long as Penix is healthy.

And Brian Robinson Jr. had himself a night, turning 15 opportunities into 67 yards and three touchdowns. He has double-digit touches in each of his past three games and has four total touchdowns in the past two games. Robinson should be added off the waiver wire if he is out there. Not only is he one of the top insurance backs, but he is carving out a role with standalone value. He can be a flex option with byes coming up and due to all the injuries.

What else you need to know from 'Monday Night Football':

Chris Olave continues to produce at an extremely high level. He turned 12 targets into eight catches for 116 yards Monday and has topped 19 fantasy points in every game. Outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Amon-Ra St. Brown, there are not many receivers I would rather have.
It was a tough game for Tyler Shough, who was able to salvage his fantasy night with a last-drive touchdown pass. He finished with 286 yards and the touchdown, failing to top 22 fantasy points for the first time this season (15.94). Still, Shough is in play outside of the tough matchups. But he has just that next week against the Minnesota Vikings, so fantasy managers may want to look at their other options.
Alvin Kamara led the way in the backfield for the Saints with 41% of the snaps, posting seven carries and seven targets. He turned those into 58 yards and two touchdowns. While it is tough to bank on big yardage from Kamara, the pass-game work paired with goal-line usage keeps him in play as a RB2 or flex option.
Juwan Johnson and Devaughn Vele continue to produce for the Saints. Johnson turned eight targets into six catches for 59 yards. He has double-digit fantasy points in every game and is the TE3 on the season. He has earned his way into starting lineups weekly. Vele finished with six catches, 54 yards and a touchdown on nine targets. He has topped 11 fantasy points three times. Vele is a high-floor option who can be started most weeks until rookie Jordyn Tyson returns.
Kendre Miller fumbled and the Saints turned to rookie CJ Donaldson late. While Kamara is the only Saints RB you can use for fantasy right now, this RB2 battle is one to monitor moving forward.

Oct. 5: Who did -- or didn't -- get the ball Sunday?

The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out to me.

By Eric Moody

Indianapolis Colts vs. Washington Commanders

Rachaad White's shoulder injury gave Jacory Croskey-Merritt a chance to take control of the backfield, but that didn't happen. He finished with 11 touches for 50 total yards and 7.0 fantasy points. Austin Ekeler got more involved as the game went on, finishing with five touches for 40 yards and 5.0 points while splitting early-down snaps with Croskey-Merritt in the second half. Ekeler is worth adding in deeper leagues, while Croskey-Merritt is tougher to trust. Kaytron Allen had just three touches for one yard, with Ekeler and Craig Reynolds both playing ahead of him.

New England Patriots at Buffalo Bills

James Cook III finished with 14 touches and 16.3 fantasy points against the Patriots, but it's worth noting that he set a season-low snap total. Ty Johnson continues to handle much of the passing-game and third-down work. This game was never separated by more than one score, so Cook finishing with only 14 touches is worth monitoring. He remains an RB1, but fantasy managers should keep an eye on his usage.

Rhamondre Stevenson left late with a right knee injury, but he was able to walk off under his own power. Before that, he remained the more valuable fantasy back in New England's rotation. Stevenson finished with 16 touches and 18.4 fantasy points, while TreVeyon Henderson had 14 touches for 42 yards and 4.2 points. Stevenson also continued to get the more valuable third-down, two-minute, short-yardage and goal-line work, while leading the Patriots' backfield in snaps, routes, touches and fantasy points.

New York Jets at Chicago Bears

Braelon Allen handled nearly all of the work with Breece Hall out. He played 93% of the Jets' offensive snaps, took all 14 carries and caught both of his targets. Isaiah Davis played just two snaps and didn't get a touch. The fantasy production wasn't huge, but the usage was exactly what managers wanted to see. If Hall remains out, Allen should continue to handle the bulk of the backfield work. It's worth noting that the Jets possessed the ball for just 17:15, their lowest time of possession in a game since Week 16 of the 2005 season, which helps explain why Allen's final touch total wasn't higher.

Kenyon Sadiq was held without a catch, but he did see four targets. More importantly, his snap rate and route participation both increased from Week 3 to Week 4. That's encouraging considering the Jets' low time of possession. It's also worth noting that none of Sadiq's targets were catchable. Looking ahead, the Jets face a Browns defense in Week 5 that has allowed the eighth-most receiving yards to tight ends. Sadiq remains a must-hold player.

Kyle Monangai took over after D'Andre Swift lost a fumble and finished with 30 carries, two touchdowns and 28.0 fantasy points. Swift still handled 15 carries before the benching, so Chicago's backfield remains a committee for now. Monangai's workload shows the upside if Swift misses time or loses more work. Swift remains an RB2, while Monangai is a flex with upside and would move into the RB1 conversation if he became the lead back. It's also worth noting that the Bears possessed the ball for 42:45, their highest time of possession in a game since 1994, which helped create an unusually large number of rushing attempts.

Jacksonville Jaguars at Cincinnati Bengals

Chase Brown continued to dominate Cincinnati's backfield, playing a season-high share of the snaps and finishing with 20 touches and a season-high 19.1 fantasy points. He managed just 10 yards on nine carries, but his receiving role saved the day with 11 catches for 71 yards on 11 targets. Brown also handled more third-down work than usual and led the backfield in routes run. The rushing production was ugly, but this kind of workload keeps him firmly in the RB1 conversation. He gets a great matchup in Week 5 against a Dolphins defense that has allowed the most fantasy points per game to running backs.

Brian Thomas Jr. set season highs in snap rate and fantasy points (9.7), with a receiving touchdown helping his production against the Bengals. Jacksonville's increased use of 11 personnel also helped boost his playing time. Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers remain the top two receivers, but Thomas mixed into 12 personnel more than he had previously. His role is moving in the right direction, although he's still difficult to trust in fantasy lineups.

Brenton Strange set a season high in snaps and turned the expanded role into eight targets and 16.5 fantasy points, both season highs. Jacksonville's increased use of 11 personnel helped boost his playing time, while the favorable matchup against a Bengals defense that has allowed the fifth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends also contributed to the production.

Arizona Cardinals at New York Giants

Cam Skattebo is still the Giants' lead back and finished with 19 touches against the Cardinals, but the workload is becoming less concentrated. Tyrone Tracy Jr. handled most of the third-down snaps, while Najee Harris also rotated in on early downs. Skattebo's early-down involvement fell to a season low. He still led the Giants' backfield with 7.6 fantasy points, but averaged just 3.2 yards per carry.

Marvin Harrison Jr. finished with a season-high 8.2 fantasy points thanks to a receiving touchdown, but his playing time continues to trend down, and he set a season low in snaps against the Giants. Trey McBride (46) and Michael Wilson (44) have dominated Arizona's targets this season, while Harrison Jr. has just 13.

Los Angeles Rams at Philadelphia Eagles

Dontayvion Wicks had a chance to take on a bigger role with DeVonta Smith out, but it didn't lead to much fantasy production. He led Eagles pass catchers in snaps and routes but finished with just five targets and a season-low 4.8 fantasy points. Darius Cooper made more of his opportunity, finishing with season highs in targets (7) and fantasy points (18.3).

Green Bay Packers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

The Packers leaned more heavily on 13 personnel against the Buccaneers, which helped Tucker Kraft stay on the field and finish with seven targets and 16.5 fantasy points. Matthew Golden also saw seven targets and scored 11.5 points. Christian Watson, meanwhile, saw his snaps dip to a season low and finished with just three targets and 7.7 fantasy points as Green Bay leaned more on 13 personnel.

Tennessee Titans at Baltimore Ravens

Carnell Tate finished with season highs in both targets (12) and fantasy points (21.5) against the Ravens. He led all Titans skill-position players in snaps, routes and targets. Tate's 145 receiving yards were the most in a game by a Titans rookie since A.J. Brown had 153 against the Raiders in 2019. Tate remains on the flex radar with upside in Week 5 against a Texans defense that has allowed the second-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers.

Tony Pollard continues to lead the Titans' backfield in touches this season, and that was the case again against the Ravens. He's had at least 18 touches and scored at least 13 fantasy points in back-to-back games. Pollard is firmly on the flex radar in Week 5 against a tough Texans matchup, then gets a more favorable spot in Week 6 against a Colts defense that has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to running backs.

Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans

The Texans changed the timing of their backfield rotation in Week 4. David Montgomery had typically handled the opening two possessions, but Woody Marks checked in on the second drive against the Cowboys. Montgomery still led the backfield in snaps and touches (10), but Marks finished with more fantasy points thanks to a rushing touchdown. Marks is also getting involved earlier in games and may be working his way into a larger weekly role.

Miami Dolphins at Minnesota Vikings

Ollie Gordon II may have moved to the top of the Dolphins backfield following De'Von Achane's season ending injury. Jaylen Wright started the game, but he struggled early as Miami rotated the backs by series. Gordon took over in the second half and finished the game leading the backfield in snaps, routes, touches (11) and fantasy points (18). He rushed for a career-high 100 yards.

Aaron Jones Sr. has continued to dominate snaps, routes and touches in the Vikings' backfield over the last three weeks with Jordan Mason on injured reserve. He finished with the second-most targets on the team (8), behind only T.J. Hockenson, who had 13. Jones also set a season high with 23 touches against the Dolphins and has scored at least 10 fantasy points in four straight games, including a season-high 16.8 in Week 4.

Kansas City Chiefs at Las Vegas Raiders

Kenneth Walker III has had at least 20 touches and scored at least 21 fantasy points in every game this season. However, Walker's route participation has dropped in each of the last two weeks. Walker has just three targets over that stretch after seeing 16 through the first two games. The production is still there, but the dip in passing-game work is worth watching.

Denver Broncos at San Francisco 49ers

George Kittle's playing time has increased each week, and that trend continued against the Broncos, when he played over 90% of the snaps. He's now scored at least 17 fantasy points in three straight games. Entering Monday, Kittle is the TE2 in fantasy and has been an excellent value relative to where he was drafted this summer.

Los Angeles Chargers at Seattle Seahawks

Omarion Hampton continues to disappoint because the Chargers are splitting the backfield almost evenly among three players. Hampton, Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal all played between 25 and 26 snaps on Sunday. Mitchell led the group with 15 touches, while Hampton had 11 and Vidal seven. Hampton scored a rushing touchdown and 13.3 fantasy points, Vidal had a receiving touchdown and 11.6, while Mitchell finished with 11.3. That kind of split puts a real cap on Hampton's weekly ceiling.

Detroit Lions at Carolina Panthers

Tetairoa McMillan scored 45.2 fantasy points against the Lions, the highest total by any player this season, with Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette sidelined. He led the Panthers in routes and targets, but the most interesting development was his production from the slot, where he was targeted heavily and generated nearly half of his fantasy points. It will be worth watching whether that usage continues once Coker and Legette return after Carolina's Week 5 bye.

Sam LaPorta finished with 13 targets and 22.4 fantasy points, leading the Lions in both categories as Detroit leaned heavily on the passing game. However, he ran the fourth-most routes among Lions pass catchers as his playing time in 11 personnel dipped. That's something to monitor if Detroit finds itself in more neutral or positive game scripts, although this defense has allowed the most yards and points per game to opponents.

stories.headline: George Russell and Kimi Antonelli to run different Mercedes packages at Singapore Grand Prix
stories.summary: Title rivals Kimi Antonelli and George Russell will drive different specifications of Mercedes' Formula 1 car at this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix as the team searches for answers over its lack of performance in Malaysia.
stories.body:
Title rivals Kimi Antonelli and George Russell will drive different specifications of Mercedes' Formula 1 car at this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix as the team searches for answers over its lack of performance in Malaysia.

Antonelli will run the upgraded aerodynamic package that the team debuted last weekend, while Russell will revert to the previous specification that won races in Monza, Madrid and Baku.

The team hopes that running a comparison between the two cars will help it understand why the new package did not perform as expected in Malaysia and allow it to define a longer-term development direction.

Russell is Antonelli's closest rival in this year's drivers' championship, although a power unit failure in Malaysia saw him fall 84 points behind his teammate in the standings.

Russell claims he pushed for the two cars to run different specifications this weekend as soon as it became clear in Malaysia that the new package was not performing.

He said the decision then became a "no-brainer" when his power unit failure on Sunday meant he would be starting from the back of the grid in Singapore due to an engine penalty.

"Actually, I instigated the conversation prior to the race [in Malaysia] on Sunday," Russell said. "So when the failure happened it was kind of a no-brainer because we were 50-50 about it pre-race and I was more in favour to do it, and now it is a total no-brainer."

Russell suspects the lack of performance compared to rivals Red Bull in Malaysia was more track specific than a direct result of the upgrade, but welcomed the opportunity to return to the car specification he won with at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix two weeks ago.

"We're pretty confident it [the lack of performance] is Malaysia specific," he said. "When you look at the pace of Red Bull as well, they clearly overperformed compared to where they've been this season compared to all of the other teams.

"And actually when you look at our pace compared to McLaren and Ferrari it wasn't too dissimilar, it wasn't massively out of bed.

"So with this engine penalty this weekend has just given them a good opportunity to roll back, it's the car that I won in Baku with, so yeah that's it."

The upgrade package is the result of months of development work after Mercedes opted not to keep pace with the updates of its rivals and instead work towards a single significant step for the final third of the season.

The upgrades to the car are far-reaching, including a new floor, rear suspension, and noticeable changes to the upper bodywork of the car, including its engine cover.

Antonelli believes the upgrade ultimately has more potential but still requires setup work to unlock it.

"It's just a matter of trying to put the car in the right window and understand it more," he said. "And this weekend, I think, is a good example. It's going to be a good opportunity to see and to compare the two packages, because we know the old one -- we've known it for ages.

"We know how to set up the car around that package, we know it works really well and it's really fast in these kind of tracks.

"And, you know, we really want to understand, on the other hand, this new package and trying to really extract the maximum out of it, because the team has done a tremendous job. They're doing so much work on this new package and it would be just a shame to write it off so early.

"So I feel like I'm quite comfortable on keeping it. And actually, you know, I really want to help the team out to understand it more and to, as I said before, try to extract the potential."

stories.headline: Wysh List: What NHL execs think of ESPN's top 100 player rankings
stories.summary: Who was too high or too low according to actual team personnel and players? Plus, winners and losers of the week, key upcoming games and more.
stories.body:
"Why do you do this to yourselves?"

That was the first reaction from an NHL general manager as he perused the latest NHL Rank, the top 100 player list that publishes at the start of every season. It was a reaction that signaled some discontent with the ranking -- and he wasn't alone -- as well as a twinge of sympathy for the inevitable backlash that accompanies such an undertaking.

Here's the method to this madness: 15 individuals from the ESPN hockey family, from front-facing talents to ink-drenched scribes to analytics virtuosi, submitted their own ranking of the top 100 NHL players based on how well they're expected to perform in the 2026-27 regular season. Those ballots are combined to come up with a final Top 100.

So, in theory, this is a projection of greatness rather than a coronation for past efforts. Does that explain why Connor Hellebuyck, currently suspended by the Winnipeg Jets after a trade request, could be ranked 22nd if he's not even playing? Well, no, it doesn't, but then there are plenty of other questions for those who debated it this week.

I spoke with several NHL executives about this year's ranking. They had questions of their own.

"Why is Alex Ovechkin ranked here? Like, at all?" one executive asked.

The Washington Capitals' captain was ranked No. 78.

"He barely skates anymore. Ovechkin being on this list is silly. What year is this?"

Oh, c'mon ... let the man retire with dignity!

Another NHL executive believed there was another glaring gaffe in the ranking: New York Islanders phenom Matthew Schaefer at No. 16. Last season's rookie of the year had 59 points in 82 games while skating 24:41 per night. That ice time ranked 14th among all defensemen, and many of those defensemen who skated more finished well behind the 19-year-old in this ranking.

"Not many young defensemen have that kind of impact, that early," they said.

Speaking of Schaefer: "So two of the top six defensemen in the NHL got cut by Hockey Canada? Because Colton Parayko, Travis Sanheim and Drew Doughty are nowhere to be found on this list, and they all played in the Olympics," pondered one NHL executive, in reference to Schaefer and Evan Bouchard of the Edmonton Oilers.

(For what it's worth, Doughty made last year's list at No. 54 while the others did not.)

A few other reactions to our player ranking from NHL front office suits:

Two execs believed that the voters had succumbed to the siren's song of scoring, rather than accounting for the actual sway players have over their team's fortunes. "I think you have some high rankings on players who have more points scored than actual impact," one GM said. Another team exec lamented: "Too many empty-calorie point guys that don't drive winning," while specifically calling out Montreal winger Cole Caufield (25th).
A few players were cited by multiple NHL executives as being undervalued in this ranking: New York Rangers defenseman Adam Fox (51), Vegas Golden Knights winger Mark Stone (73) and Tampa Bay Lightning winger Brandon Hagel (55). "Brandon Hagel is a superstar, and people don't realize it. Way too low," one executive said.
More than one exec noted that our ranking of the 100 best players didn't exactly honor the reigning Stanley Cup champions, the Carolina Hurricanes. Center Sebastian Aho (48) was the only Cane to crack the top 50, and he was down from 28th on last year's list. Jaccob Slavin (62), Seth Jarvis (74), Andrei Svechnikov (84) and Nikolaj Ehlers (96) also made the cut. "Where's anyone from the best line from the reigning Cup winners?" one executive asked, referring to the trio of Taylor Hall, Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake.

I'm not going to deny there are a few shots that missed the net on this list. Schaefer is way too high. So is Martin Necas of the Colorado Avalanche at 24th; he had a career year skating 82% of the time with Nathan MacKinnon -- a luxury not afforded to several wingers ranked behind him. Would I have Brandt Clarke ranked ahead of Shea Theodore? I would not. Would I have had Darren Raddysh on this list at all, let alone at No. 90? I also would not.

On the flippity flop, Leo Carlson (36th) and Stone should be much higher. I would have liked Florida defenseman Seth Jones somewhere on this list -- although perhaps the toxic stink cloud from his time with the Blackhawks still follows him in South Florida despite helping the Panthers to their second Stanley Cup win.

But here's my scorching hot take on this year's NHL Rank on ESPN. Prepare yourself. Maybe get a tall glass of milk to handle the ghost pepper sear of this take.

The NHL Rank list is overall pretty ... good?

Qualms and quibbles aside, the top of the list seems about right. Proper respect was given to emerging talents (Macklin Celebrini at No. 4 and Nick Suzuki at No. 19) and established stars (Sidney Crosby, hanging tough at No. 23). Heck, we even found a way to get Evgeni Malkin in at No. 100, so Pittsburgh fans can finally extinguish the torches they light whenever this ranking dropped without him in it.

During my conversations around the league about the list, I found out I wasn't alone.

"This looks absolutely fine to me. I've got nothing to criticize here," one NHL assistant general manager said.

An NHL veteran player who scanned the list agreed.

"I think everyone is actually where they should be," the player said when shown the top 100. "It's a nice list. No notes."

Based on my texts, my inbox and my mentions, everyone else had more than enough notes to share. Some even without profanity!

Jump ahead:

Winners, losers of the week

Favorite on-ice moment

Must-see games

Puck headlines

WINNERS AND LOSERS
Winner: Alex Ovechkin
Last season, Ovechkin explicitly didn't want a farewell tour because he felt his pursuit of Wayne Gretzky's record in 2024-25 overshadowed everything about the Capitals, including his teammates. But after deciding in the summer that this season would be his last in the NHL, Ovi decided to just put the issue to bed early, sparing his teammates from questions about his status for the next 80-plus games.

It also sets up the NHL for a one-of-a-kind farewell tour. Consider other recent transcendent stars. Wayne Gretzky didn't let his fate be known until there were just a few games left in the 1998-99 season. Mario Lemieux played until he couldn't. Jaromir Jagr was an afterthought on the Calgary Flames before spending the next decade in Kladno, Czechia. Ovechkin will visit 31 other teams for the final time, giving fans the chance to react to his last NHL days.

That includes what could be the emotional apex of his season on April 4 in Washington's home finale against Sidney Crosby, Evgeni Malkin and the Pittsburgh Penguins. If you don't have tickets and want to attend, prepare to sell a kidney.

Loser: Brady Tkachuk
The Florida Panthers didn't have a regulation loss in their first four games (2-0-2). Their losses were on the roster. Aleksander Barkov's lower-body injury thankfully wasn't as bad as feared, but their best player is still on the shelf for about six weeks. Brad Marchand was helped off the ice Tuesday after collisions with the net and the boards in Los Angeles. As of this writing, his status was unknown, but it didn't look good.

Another point of concern through four games: Brady Tkachuk has put out more podcasts (two) than put up points (zero), despite leading the Panthers with 11 shots. Granted, the loss of Barkov in Game 2 affected him -- witness Sam Reinhart also sporting goose eggs on his stat line through four games -- but Tkachuk was acquired to help the Panthers through significant lineup losses like they had last season. Plus, he has had to watch his old friends in Ottawa thriving in his absence.

Tkachuk will be fine. But it's not the start he or the Panthers wanted statistically.

Winner: GQ covers hockey
It's always interesting to see how a writer who doesn't cover hockey processes our silly little sport. Nick Remsen of GQ profiled San Jose Sharks star Macklin Celebrini, and gave NHL fans some artful new descriptions of backhand shots ("[He] pushed the puck into the net with the convex side of his blade, body twisting with near balletic torque...") and routine goal celebrations ("He was so happy after ricocheting a puck into the net's far outer edge that he all but flung himself into the sideboards...").

Loser: GQ makes it weird
Given the "Heated Rivalry" and "Off Campus" phenomenon and the NHL's now shuttered "Hot For Hockey" experiment, it's not out of bounds to ask someone like Macklin about the para-social relationship between fans and players. Where things got weird in the Celebrini profile: Asking about the "fan fiction element" in his fandom. Given the content in some of those stories, that question felt invasive and put him in an awkward spot.

Celebrini understandably punted on the answer, which isn't something for which he should have to answer anyway. Besides, it's not as if fan fiction involving NHL players started with Macklin Celebrini.

Winner: Dylan Larkin drama
A few sources around the league I spoke with previously didn't believe we'd see Larkin wear a Detroit sweater again, but the now-former Red Wings captain returned to the lineup from injury Tuesday night, his first game since requesting a trade from Detroit. The fans booed him as they booed him on opening night when he was introduced in street clothes; Larkin responded with a goal and an assist to reignite the dormant Detroit offense.

There were some cheers interspersed with the boos when he was announced as the No. 1 star. After the game, Larkin said, "I'm just happy to be a hockey player today and go out and try to help the team win."

Give Larkin this credit: He has spoken to reporters. He has faced the fans. He wore a uniform that he has asked to no longer wear. How this all ends up is anyone's guess, but we're here for the soap opera: "As The Winged Wheel Turns."

Loser: No-trade clauses
The aftermath of Larkin's trade request was put into sharp relief last week when NHL commissioner Gary Bettman said the league is monitoring how players are using their no-movement and no-trade clauses. Larkin, then Detroit's captain, asked out with five years left on an eight-year contract, and limited the field of suitors to three teams with his no-trade clause.

Just like how the NHL enacted offside reviews because one player (Matt Duchene) was a country mile offside and the officials missed it, Larkin's trade request appears to have lit the fuse for this potentially contentious labor dispute.

What I can report: Bettman is speaking to players to get feedback on the way trade protection is currently being used and potential changes to the system down the line. It'll be fascinating to hear how they feel about Larkin's gambit.

Favorite on-ice moment

It's always fascinating to see what the league's preeminent agitators use for material. Ottawa forward Nick Cousins pantomiming the letter "C" and pointing to his chest as he taunts Dylan Larkin getting the captaincy stripped from him? Chef's kiss, especially if you want to add the subtext of having reminded Larkin that he's stuck in some kind of trade demand purgatory.

Must-see games coming up

Toronto Maple Leafs at Vegas Golden Knights

Thursday, 10 p.m. ET | ESPN+

The vibes are good for the Leafs. They're 2-2-0. Auston Matthews scored an overtime winner against Nashville in a game that saw No. 1 pick Gavin McKenna finally hit the scoresheet. But starting with this game against old pal Mitch Marner and the Golden Knights, we're going to learn about more about Toronto: The Leafs are at Colorado, at Utah and then get Buffalo at home.

Edmonton Oilers at San Jose Sharks

Saturday, 4 p.m. ET | ESPN+

Celebrini is day-to-day, and one hopes he's available for a showdown against Connor McDavid. But no matter his status: This is a four-point divisional game for the Sharks, and if they're going to be a playoff team then these are the games they need to win.

Colorado Avalanche at Dallas Stars

Tuesday, 8:30 p.m. ET | ESPN

The first meeting between the two best regular-season teams in the Central Division last season. Three of their four games in 2025-26 went to a shootout. An early test for both teams.

From your hockey friends at ESPN

Ryan Clark went to Houston to find out why that city believes it deserves an NHL expansion team more than Austin, Texas, does. Said Mayor John Whitmire on what the city will do to get a team: "We're not going to start selling dope out of an arena or anything. But if it's lawful, we'll pull that trigger."
Sean Allen looks at hits and blocks in fantasy hockey, and who could be the most valuable players this season to that end.
Kalan Hooks with a wild story out of New Jersey, as a youth hockey team owner is under fire after threatening to suspend the children on his under-10 hockey team after their parents created their own merchandise.
Finally, Rachel Kryshak has a deep dive into which NCAA teams have the most high-end talent. How did we end up with so many kids named "Ryker" playing hockey?

Jersey Foul

I appreciate the integration of Larkin's name into this Protest Jersey about his trade request. Much more impressive than just using the "L" and taping the word "LOSER" on the back or just covering the whole thing with the word "TRAITOR," which is what other fans decided to do.

Puck headlines
DATELINE: TEAM USA GROUP CHAT
One of the greatest bits of hockey lore going these days is the power of the U.S. men's Olympic team group chat, which has been credited with having players like Winnipeg Jets goalie Connor Hellebuyck demand a trade to the U.S.

Gold medalist Vincent Trocheck of the Utah Mammoth says he believes its power is overstated.

"I think people make it a bigger thing than it is," he told me this week. "Obviously, people want the headlines, but the whole Canada thing or guys wanting out of Canada that are from the U.S., I think it was more situational than it was anything else."

But is there a thriving group chat among the players?

"There's one from Team USA. But not, like, a trade talk one," he said. "It's been dormant for a little bit. It's sad. I might have to fire it back up."

DATELINE: CONNOR HELLEBUYCK
It was a bit surprising when Jets GM Kevin Cheveldayoff didn't rule out the possibility that Hellebuyck could remain with the team after going public with a trade demand.

But one former teammate of the star goaltender I spoke with actually didn't rule it out.

The thinking here: Hellebuyck will eventually grow frustrated with losing pay after having been suspended by the Jets, as it has been reported he'll lose around $39,000 a day. But more than that, he's still on friendly terms with his teammates -- some of them neighbors -- who theoretically would welcome back the multitime Vezina Trophy winner if he decides to pull a Larkin and suit up again.

DATELINE: UTAH MAMMOTH
One sign the Mammoth are really starting to thrive in Salt Lake City? The lack of enemy fans in the stands. Team president Chris Armstrong told me that when Utah opened its season against the Blackhawks at home, there were very few Chicago fans in the building "in comparison to the inaugural season" in Salt Lake City.

"I feel like maybe that people are switching their allegiance to the Mammoth now," Armstrong said.

If they keep playing the way they're playing to start the season, who wouldn't?

The Wysh List is created by senior writer Greg Wyshynski and appears every Thursday on ESPN.com and the ESPN app.

stories.headline: Rockets, Mavs take China: Highlights, top scenes from off the court
stories.summary: The top sights and sounds from the Dallas Mavericks and Houston Rockets' preseason trip to China.
stories.body:
The NBA preseason slate sends the Dallas Mavericks and Houston Rockets across the world for a doubleheader in Macao, China, on Oct. 9 and 11.

Houston and Dallas are the second set of teams to play in Macao. The Phoenix Suns and Brooklyn Nets competed in the gambling hub last season, marking the return of the NBA to China after a yearslong hiatus. Similar to last year, the Rockets and Mavericks will be playing at Macao's Venetian Arena.

A trip overseas tends to bring a team closer together ahead of the long grind of the regular season. While the preseason action might not indicate how a team performs when the games begin to count, it's the off-court activities that can make an impact in the end.

Here's a look at the top sights and sounds from the Rockets-Mavericks trip in Macao.

A hometown welcome

With a flight time that can reach or exceed 20 hours, finally touching ground can be a relief. When each respective team arrived at their hotels, fans made sure to show the players love.

Room tour from an unlikely source

Rockets' fans got an inside look at the rooms for each player courtesy of big man Steven Adams. The 6-foot-11 center shared a video of his setup, which included a bowl of fruit, Rockets-themed pillow and Egyptian cotton.

Picture-perfect setting and love for Kyrie and Durant

It's not a trip to a new location without a memorable group photo. The Mavericks and Rockets separately posed near a body of water with the Venetian Macao set in the background.

As Dallas snapped its picture, fans flocked to greet the team -- specifically, star guard Kyrie Irving. The same occurred for Houston star Kevin Durant.

Mavs making presence felt

After the first practice in Macao for the Mavericks, the team already needed to find replacements for two items: a chair and a rim. Forward Naji Marshall broke a rim, explaining "I'm too strong and I've got too much power," before he signed it and the team collected it. Marshall then broke a chair while sitting down.

Adams and Bogdanović take in Macao

The Rockets center and his teammate Bogdan Bogdanović made sure to look around Macao to get a feel for the city. They went to the ruins of Saint Paul's, which is the facade of what was originally the church of Mater Dei built between 1602 to 1640. The duo then had some street food, all while a huge crowd followed along.

Views from Hong Kong

It takes 55 minutes to an hour to travel from Macao to Hong Kong via a ferry. A Dallas quartet of Daniel Gafford, Caleb Martin, Dwight Powell and Sergio de Larrea took advantage of the distance. The group traveled to Victoria Peak in Hong Kong.

Yao Ming ... is still growing?

The Rockets legend visited the NBA Macao house with fellow Rockets great Cuttino Mobley. While at the venue, Mobley found a cardboard cutout of the 7-foot-6 center. Remarkably, when Yao approached it, it seemed like he had grown. He joked: "I have something in my shoes."

KD, Kyrie hang out

The two future Hall of Famers shared a moment together on the court in Macao, chatting it up and laughing.

For the kids
Young fans were more than thrilled to meet their heroes in Macao, and both Durant and Flagg were happy to oblige.

stories.headline: Liberty, refs at odds postgame over reset timeout in Game 2
stories.summary: Breanna Stewart said officials told her the Liberty did not have a reset timeout to use at the end of overtime in Wednesday's loss at Atlanta. Crew chief Fatou Cissoko-Stephens disputed this in a pool report, saying the remaining timeout was communicated.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- The Atlanta Dream took a commanding 2-0 series lead over the New York Liberty behind a 101-98 overtime win Wednesday, positioning them one win away from the WNBA Finals.

But the evening finished rife with controversy after two-time WNBA MVP Breanna Stewart said in the postgame news conference that the officials told her the team did not have a reset timeout to use at the end of the game when they actually did have one.

"This is not blaming the refs, but when I ask both refs if we have a reset timeout at the end, and they tell us no, and then we leave the game with the reset timeout, it's pretty frustrating," Stewart said.

She continued later: "I asked Kevin [Fahy]. I said, 'Do we have a reset timeout?' And he said, 'I'm going to check at the table.' So then he looked to [crew chief] Fatou [Cissoko-Stephens], and she said, 'No.' So then he told me, 'No.'"

During overtime, each team receives two team timeouts and one reset timeout, which allows the team to advance the ball without huddling on the sideline.

After a late turnover by New York, the Liberty sent Angel Reese to the free throw line, where she made both free throws to put the Dream ahead by three points. New York then inbounded the ball from under its own basket, and while Stewart was able to manage a last-ditch heave, it fell short of the basket.

"Of course, who knows what happened to end the game," Stewart said. "But we would have had hopefully a better shot on our goal."

The Liberty have made an official inquiry with the league into the situation, a source told ESPN.

As part of the pool report -- with officials not made available to reporters until nearly two hours after the game concluded -- ESPN asked Cissoko-Stephens why Stewart said she was told the Liberty did not have a reset timeout available.

"Stewart was standing behind referee Fahy when he confirmed with his partner between Reese's penalty free throws that New York did indeed have a reset timeout remaining," she said.

When asked whether he was unaware if the team had its reset timeout, Liberty coach Chris DeMarco responded, "Yeah, same thing. They just said we didn't have it. Multiple staff members [were told]. It is what it is. We've got to demand more. But it is what it is."

Cissoko-Stephens then said there was no communication between the officials and anyone else on the team.

Dream coach Karl Smesko said he was aware the Liberty had a timeout left.

"I was, I thought they had a timeout left," Smesko said. "But they played it out the way they did. So I was expecting it to be advanced, but it wasn't, so we had to play it, and fortunately we were able to get the stop."

Cissoko-Stephens clarified that available timeouts are tracked by the scorer's table and statistical staff, but that "teams are responsible for managing and tracking their timeout usage throughout the game."

Calling a timeout that a team does not have would result in a technical foul.

But there was plenty in the Liberty's control that didn't go their way.

Most significantly, with New York down one with less than 10 seconds left in overtime, Sabrina Ionescu inadvertently threw the ball out of bounds while driving. She had corralled the ball after New York retained possession following a jump ball that was called when three Atlanta defenders collapsed on Jonquel Jones in the paint.

"I told them it was my fault," Ionescu said. "I took ownership for that. This loss is on me. I've got to take it on the chin, and I've got to be better."

A defensive breakdown before Ionescu's play led to Naz Hillmon getting an open layup with 20.8 seconds left and what ended up being the Dream's go-ahead basket.

The Dream had six players finish in double figures, led by 23 points apiece from Reese and Jordin Canada. Stewart, Jones and Marine Fauthoux combined for 76 of New York's 98 points.

But the Liberty also turned the ball over 17 times, with the Dream scoring 28 points off those turnovers; New York took 64 shots and Atlanta attempted 84.

"There were times when we were up and then we'd turn it over or [have an] empty possessions or just lapses on defense that [they'd] just back cut, we just gave them a layup," Ionescu said. "So there's obviously so many [plays] when you kind of start to think about it that costs you a game. It's not just like one reset or whatever the story is going to be."

Added Leonie Fiebich: "I think we all f---ed up at some stage throughout the game."

It wasn't all bad for the Liberty, as Fauthoux, a rookie point guard, forced overtime with a 3-pointer with 10.3 seconds left in regulation -- though the Dream nearly won in regulation with Rhyne Howard's last-second shot on the ensuing play just rolling out of the basket.

No team has ever come back from down from a 2-0 deficit to win a best-of-five series in WNBA history.

"I do think we came with the right mindset," DeMarco said. "We were physical. Not blaming anybody. End of the day, we had our chances. They had a layup late. We missed a few rebounds we could have come up with, but the series is not over. The series is not over, and we believe in ourselves, and we believe in this team going forward."

stories.headline: Harry Kane arrival would be 'fulfilment of a dream' - MLS commissioner
stories.summary: MLS commissioner Don Garber would love Harry Kane to follow Lionel Messi across the pond and says the England skipper's interest helps fulfil a dream that Sir David Beckham kept alive.
stories.body:
MLS commissioner Don Garber would love Harry Kane to follow Lionel Messi across the pond and says the England skipper's interest helps fulfil a dream that Sir David Beckham kept alive.

The 33-year-old is in the running for the Ballon d'Or having scored 73 goals for club and country in a season that saw the striker win the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich before World Cup bronze.

Kane shows no signs of slowing and he marked his record-equalling 125th England appearance by extending his international goal tally to 91 in Tuesday's 3-0 Nations League win against Czechia.

The striker scored six goals across a four-match camp that began with him revealing his interest in eventually moving to MLS as the striker spoke about his dreams of being an NFL kicker.

"I'd love for him to do that," commissioner Garber said. "I think, for me, it is the fulfilment of the dream that we had to build a proper soccer league that would drive a soccer nation. That sounds colloquial but actually we have that written down.

"We wanted to create something that would have the Harry Kanes of the world say 'I'd kind of like to play in MLS.' And I think Messi proved that.

"That was a competitive process, working to ensure that we had a dynamic that would be better than going back to Barca, working a dynamic that would not have him want to play in Saudi Arabia.

"Play in Miami, have them be able to build a new stadium and have him set records and be an MVP, and then have an unbelievable goodbye [this week] from his international career."

Garber welcomes Kane's keenness to move to MLS and is eternally grateful to another England captain as he prepares to step down from the post of commissioner he has held since 1999.

Beckham's move to LA Galaxy acted as the catalyst for the league's growth, which only accelerated when the former midfielder helped form Inter Miami and sign Argentina great Messi in 2023.

"I don't think I would say one is more important than the other," Garber said of the star duo's impact.

"David put this league on the path to credibility and respect. In the prime of his career, he came to LA.

"He came into Major League Soccer and showed the world that this league can be competitive, it could be respected, it could be fun, it could have great players.

"It attracted [Thierry] Henry and many, many other players right after that, so without David there's probably no Major League Soccer.

"That being said, Major League Soccer would not be the global phenomenon and not be sort of on the hearts and minds of just about anybody in the world without Leo Messi."

Garber will become chairman at the turn of the year and is proud of his legacy with MLS, which was founded as part of the bid to hold the 1994 World Cup in a country that has just co-hosted the largest edition of the tournament.

- Harry Kane is England's greatest ever player - Jude Bellingham

- Harry Kane's England milestones: From his first cap to becoming all-time record goalscorer

- England Nations League takeaways: Kane makes history, Tuchel steadies ship

The 68-year-old says they have made the planet's "biggest commercial market for the sport" during that time and is excited to see how they build on firm foundations.

"We just went from a country road, now we're getting onto the highway," Garber told the Press Association. "And we've got to get better.

"We have to have a league that is more competitive, that has an ability to get into the Club World Cup and win games. Miami won one.

"Not just be there but have people think that an MLS team can compete against other clubs in the world."

stories.headline: Mikel Arteta: 'I still have the scar' from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat
stories.summary: Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.
stories.body:
Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.

The Spaniard, whose new four-year contract at the Emirates was announced on Wednesday, took the club to their first Champions League final for 20 years last season but saw his team defeated on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

Echoing the words of the last man to take them to the brink of elite European glory -- Arsène Wenger, who previously said that "every defeat is a scar in your heart" -- Arteta told The Athletic: "I still have the scar, like Arsène says.

"I still have that poison in my veins. It has to stay there because that's when you learn and that probably is going to be a massive driver for me and everybody."

Looking towards the future, Arteta added that he was excited for a number of different aspects of the club's growth.

"Globally, with our supporters? Great. How are we going to build the next three squads? Great. How the rules of the game are going to change us, and how we're going to stay ahead of that to take advantage? Great," he said.

"But this is going to happen if every single day we look after what we built. We make it a little bit better, like software that is upgrading and upgrading. When can it stop is infinite."

He added: "It feels like it's still a lot to do, and it's just the beginning."

Arteta has, however, already managed to do something no Arsenal manager had achieved for 22 years: win a league title.

"It wasn't just a trophy. It was a moment that we're going to remember for the rest of our lives," he said.

Asked what game from his Arsenal tenure he would relive, the 44-year-old chose the controversial 1-0 win over West Ham which put the Gunners on the brink of returning to the top of the perch.

"This is football elevated to its best version, when a journey, a moment that can change so many people's lives, goes one way or the other," he said. "You just pray because you know if it goes the wrong side, probably it's gone again.

"That day when I went home, I said, 'We're going to be champions. It is our year. This has happened for a reason, and we're going to get it done.'"

stories.headline: Saints trade ruckman to Cats, chase on for star Swan
stories.summary: Geelong have brokered a trade for St Kilda ruckman Rowan Marshall, further depleting the Cats' draft stocks as Swans defender Nick Blakey eyes a move.
stories.body:
St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No. 14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

Cats football boss Andrew Mackie on Monday indicated an unwillingness to part with their first-round pick for Marshall after the Saints asked for a player to be attached to the trade.

St Kilda football boss Lenny Hayes hailed the fair return for Marshall, who has played 177 AFL games since being a rookie pick at age 21.

"We are pleased to have achieved (adequate compensation) by bringing in another first round selection, alongside our existing pick at eight," Hayes said.

Geelong needed to bolster their ruck stocks, with Rhys Stanley retiring and 21-year-old Mitchell Edwards still finding his feet at the level.

The Cats are among five clubs eyeing Nick Blakey as the Swans defender tests the water for a possible trade.

The 2024 All-Australian was one of five players who served a club-imposed ban through the AFL finals for breaching the club's behavioural standards at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne.

The 26-year-old has since been linked to a move despite being signed to Sydney until 2031.

Swans list boss Chris Keane said the club had not been told Blakey was meeting with rival clubs this week, but remained in talks with his manager Robbie D'Orazio.

"As we sit here right now, these are all hypotheticals," he told Trade Radio.

"It's certainly not something we've actively pursued, and we feel confident that he could walk back into our footy club.

"But given the calibre of player that he is, and the fact that he is contracted for five more years, we feel like making any deal happen would be significantly challenging."

Blakey's preferred option is reportedly Geelong, but the Cats have limited draft capital after executing trades for Marshall and Essendon's Jordan Ridley.

North Melbourne have expressed interest for Blakey, whose father John played in the Kangaroos' 1996 and 1999 premierships across 224 club games.

Essendon are another suitor, with Blakey's former mentors Mark McVeigh and John Longmire joining the club and the Bombers boasting salary cap room following the exits of Zach Merrett and Ridley.

"We haven't had any indication off Nick's management that he's looking to leave Sydney," Essendon list boss Matt Rosa told Trade Radio.

"But certainly we've had some discussions internally and we'll continue to do that."

Blakey has reportedly already met with Gold Coast coach Damien Hardwick, while St Kilda are also expected to make contact.

Any trade for Blakey would likely need to be approved by a club board, given the ongoing police investigation into an alleged sexual assault at the hotel.

Swans vice-captain Isaac Heeney, star midfielder Chad Warner, tagger James Jordon and Blakey were interviewed by police but no charges have been laid.

Riley Bice, another Swan banned for round 24 and the finals campaign, is not being investigated.

In other developments, young Hawk Aidan Schubert has agreed to be traded to Gold Coast in a separate deal that is expected to allow Ben King join Hawthorn as a free agent.

The Suns' 72-hour window to match the Hawks' offer for King or accept compensation, likely pick No. 7 in the draft, ends at 4.15pm (AEDT) on Friday.

The Western Bulldogs are yet to file free agency paperwork for Port Adelaide's Zak Butters ahead of Friday afternoon's deadline.

Port can accept draft compensation, which would currently deliver pick No.5, or match the Bulldogs' offer and force a trade.

The trade period closes on Wednesday evening.

stories.headline: Silva rises in P4P women's top 10, making most of golden opportunity
stories.summary: After winning UFC women's flyweight title, Silva rises in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
The women's flyweight division might be the most stacked weight class in the UFC, and Natalia Silva wears the gold.

Silva was too fast, too precise and too elusive for Wang Cong in the UFC 332 main event on Saturday, and as a result, the 29-year-old from Brazil captured the vacant 125-pound title. She moves up one position to No. 4 in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound rankings.

Silva is one of seven flyweights in the women's top 10. The division with the next most pound-for-pound elites is lightweight, with three fighters in the men's rankings.

The top two fighters on the women's list are Valentina Shevchenko, who vacated the UFC title last month while healing shoulder and back injuries, and Zhang Weili, a two-time former strawweight titlist who last fought at flyweight, in an unsuccessful challenge of Shevchenko in November.

Aside from Silva, there are three other UFC flyweights in the top 10 (Alexa Grasso, Manon Fiorot and Erin Blanchfield), and the rankings also include PFL 125-pounder Dakota Ditcheva.

UFC women's bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison has been missing from these rankings for the past few months because, with no fights since June 2025, she is ineligible. But Harrison will return from neck surgery to defend her title against former two-division champion and consensus GOAT Amanda Nunes at UFC 334 on Nov. 14.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Oct. 7. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which Natalia Silva captured by beating Wang Cong at UFC 332. When Shevchenko is healed up, she'll be looking to take back the belt.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 21-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Wang Cong, Oct. 3

Next: TBA

Silva was looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Rose Namajunas at UFC 324. And now she has fulfilled that expectation, beating Wang at UFC 332 to win the belt vacated by injured Valentina Shevchenko. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

5. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Previous ranking: 4

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her upcoming bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.
